reuse.why: The rule change goes into the existing shared helpers getWorstCaseAmount and getExpectedAmount, which every planning path already calls.

duplication.why: Two one-line edits to the shared definitions and nothing copied.

placement.why: The change stays in shared/schedules.ts, where the worst-case rule lives.

scope.why: Only the two helper bodies, their comments and their tests change.

maintainability.why: It is minimal and clear. The one wrinkle is that getScheduledAmount (used for editing and display, with an inverse flag) also goes through getWorstCaseAmount, so it silently picks up the new min rule, and the coupling is not called out.

bypasses_abstraction.where: All changes are inside the shared amount helpers.
